note: SCOPE_1.8.9 §11 gate 2 (parity) as something a machine can check. The gate asks that Android and iOS make the same layout decisions for the same template and ride, on frame fractions. A side-by-side screenshot proves it once, for the ride and the moment it was taken; this proves it on every run, for the decisions that are shared. What is frozen here is the design space itself — the 1080-wide canvas, what each template declares, and where the route box sits as a fraction of its frame — because those are the numbers that make a template the same picture on both phones. The per-template type tables (baselines, sizes) stay private to each renderer and are covered by the render tests; this file covers the contract between them.
_design_note: Every dimension in both renderers is designed on a 1080-px-wide canvas and scaled by the width actually rendered, which is what makes a preview the export at a smaller size. A platform that changed this would need a different scale rule, not a different number.
_canvas_note: Destination-real sizes. Instagram wants 1080 × 1920 for a story and upscales anything smaller into the soft look that reads as 'made by an app'. The card is the Sticker's own frame: sized to its content, not to a destination.

templates.note: 4:5 first: detail rewards a reader who stops, and a story frame gets a second and a half.
Declared last so its appearing and disappearing never moves the others in the strip.
1.8.9 Part 2. Aggregate, not both: a single ride has no sequence, and an itinerary of one leg is a worse Trace.

_scope_note: §9.3, forced by the data: the Award has no aggregate reveal, the Instrument's splits are one continuous ride's, and N rides have N lights. The strip therefore shows five cards for a single ride and three for a selection.

trace_route_box_fractions._note: The same box as a fraction of its frame — the form §11 gate 2 states the parity in. Left and right are fractions of width, top and bottom of height. Derived, and asserted as derived: a client that changed a canvas size without moving the box would fail here rather than silently reframe the route.
